title: Year 9 end-of-half-term assessment: Lord of the Flies, non-fiction and grammar
subject: English
unit: Spring 1: Lord of the Flies (William Golding), part two
source: Written for english/y9 lesson 28 (End-of-half-term assessment and mark scheme (portal))

blocks.h: Section A: Lord of the Flies (retrieval)

questions.q: What does Ralph use the conch for?
questions.a: To call meetings; whoever holds it may speak

questions.q: What do the boys use Piggy's glasses for?
Which boy realises that the Beast is 'only us'?
Who rescues the boys at the end?

passage.title: Rules and freedom
paras: People often complain about rules, but rules are what let a group live together. A football match without rules is not freedom; it is chaos, and the strongest player wins. Good rules protect the weakest, not only the strongest.

questions.q: What is the writer's main argument?
questions.a: Rules are needed for a group to live together; they protect the weak

questions.q: How does the writer use an example to persuade?
questions.a: The football match without rules shows that no rules means 'chaos' where 'the strongest player wins'; a familiar example makes the idea concrete

questions.q: Make this more concise: 'At this point in time, the boys basically start to become really savage.'
questions.a: For example: 'Now the boys become savage.'

questions.q: Name the evaluative verb that is most precise for a writer's purpose: shows, suggests, condemns.
How does Golding present the breakdown of civilisation in Lord of the Flies? Write two PEEDL paragraphs.
questions.a: Award up to 10: two argued points (2), apt short evidence (2), analysis of methods such as symbolism (conch, fire, glasses) (3), context (post-war fears) or an alternative reading (2), link (1).
